skill.description: Complete migration guide from Prisma ORM v6 to v7 covering all breaking changes. Use when upgrading Prisma versions, encountering v7 errors, or migrating existing projects. Triggers on "upgrade to prisma 7", "prisma 7 migration", "prisma-client generator", "driver adapter required".
skill.summary: Complete migration guide from Prisma ORM v6 to v7 covering all breaking changes. Use when upgrading ...
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: This is a legitimate, Prisma-authored documentation skill guiding a Prisma ORM v6-to-v7 migration; it contains only Markdown prose and illustrative code snippets, no executable install scripts. All 268 static findings were adjudicated as false positives: the 'path traversal' hits are standard `../generated/prisma` generator output/import paths, the env_access and sensitive hits are ordinary `process.env.DATABASE_URL` / `dotenv` / `.env` documentation patterns with only ellipsis placeholders (no live secrets), and the 'shell backtick execution' hits are Markdown code fences and JavaScript template literals. One low-severity semantic note flags a troubleshooting suggestion to disable TLS certificate verification, which is clearly framed as a legacy fallback with a secure alternative offered alongside it.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance recommends disabling TLS certificate verification (`ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }`) in the driver-adapter config.
remediation.suggestion: Lead with the secure fix (configure a proper CA via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or the adapter's `ssl.ca`) and present `rejectUnauthorized: false` only as an explicit, discouraged last resort scoped to local development, warning that it disables MITM protection in production.

- `removed-features` - removed middleware, metrics, and legacy CLI behavior

semantic_findings.title: Documentation suggests disabling TLS certificate verification
semantic_findings.description: The SKILL.md troubleshooting section advises adding `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }` to the driver-adapter config to preserve old SSL behavior. Disabling certificate verification removes protection against man-in-the-middle attacks on the database connection. The advice is clearly labeled as a fallback and a secure alternative (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / proper CA configuration) is offered on the next line, so this is guidance quality rather than an exploitable code defect, but users may copy it into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure snippet is verifiably present and would weaken TLS if copied verbatim, but it is explicitly framed as a legacy workaround with a secure alternative provided immediately after, so real-world risk is limited to user misuse.

content.user_title: Migrate Prisma ORM v6 to v7 Safely
content.value_statement: Upgrading Prisma from v6 to v7 introduces breaking changes across the generator, driver adapters, config file, and module system that are easy to get wrong. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured, prioritized migration path so each breaking change is handled in the correct order.
actual_capabilities: Explains every Prisma v6-to-v7 breaking change grouped by priority, from schema generator to Accelerate.
Shows how to switch from the `prisma-client-js` generator to the new `prisma-client` generator with an explicit output path.
Documents required driver adapter setup for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Neon, and Prisma Postgres.
Covers the new `prisma.config.ts` file and manual environment variable loading with dotenv.
Details ESM-first configuration with a CommonJS fallback via `moduleFormat = "cjs"`.
Lists removed features (middleware `$use()`, metrics, legacy CLI behavior) and their replacements.
limitations: It is a reference and guidance skill; it does not run commands or modify a project automatically.
It does not cover MongoDB projects, which Prisma 7 does not support; it points to a separate skill instead.
Version-specific details are pinned to Prisma 7.6.0 and may drift as new releases ship.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an existing Prisma project
use_cases.description: A developer maintaining a Prisma v6 codebase follows the ordered steps to reach v7 without missing a breaking change.

use_cases.title: Diagnose post-upgrade errors
use_cases.description: A user hitting import or connection errors after bumping Prisma uses the troubleshooting sections to resolve them.

use_cases.title: Plan a team-wide migration
use_cases.description: A tech lead reviews the prioritized breaking-change matrix to scope and sequence a Prisma upgrade across services.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me upgrade my Prisma project from v6 to v7. Walk me through the required changes in order.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a specific error
prompt_templates.prompt: After upgrading to Prisma 7 I get a 'Cannot find module' error importing PrismaClient. What did the migration change and how do I fix it?

prompt_templates.title: Configure a driver adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: My Prisma 7 project uses PostgreSQL. Show me how to install and configure the required driver adapter and update client instantiation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Setting up driver adapters for a SQL provider

prompt_templates.title: Migrate advanced patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate my Prisma setup to v7: replace all `$use()` middleware with Client Extensions and swap `Prisma.validator()` for the `satisfies` pattern, keeping CommonJS via moduleFormat.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration of removed features and module format

output_examples.input: How do I update my schema generator block for Prisma 7?
output_examples.output: Claude explains that the default generator is now `prisma-client` (not `prisma-client-js`), that an explicit `output` path such as `../generated/prisma` is required, and that you can add `moduleFormat = "cjs"` if your app stays on CommonJS. It then shows the before-and-after generator block and reminds you to run `prisma generate`.

output_examples.input: My PostgreSQL connection broke after upgrading. What changed?
output_examples.output: Claude points out that Prisma 7 requires a driver adapter for SQL providers, walks you through installing `@prisma/adapter-pg` and `pg`, updating the client to pass the adapter, and notes that pool defaults now come from the underlying driver so you may need to set them explicitly.

best_practices: Apply the breaking changes in the documented priority order: schema, connectivity, and module system first.
Set an explicit generator `output` path and confirm it matches your import paths before running `prisma generate`.
Load environment variables explicitly with dotenv or your runtime's loader, since Prisma 7 no longer auto-loads `.env`.
anti_patterns: Applying this SQL-focused guide to a MongoDB project instead of following the dedicated MongoDB path.
Disabling TLS certificate verification (`rejectUnauthorized: false`) in production instead of configuring a proper CA.
Skipping driver adapter installation and expecting the v6 auto-connection behavior to still work.

faq.question: Which Prisma versions does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers migrating from Prisma ORM v6 to v7, pinned to the stable 7.6.0 release.

faq.question: Does it work for MongoDB projects?
faq.answer: No. Prisma 7 has no MongoDB connector. The skill tells you to keep MongoDB projects on v6 or use a separate migration path.

faq.question: Do I really need a driver adapter?
faq.answer: Yes, for SQL providers. Prisma 7 requires a driver adapter such as `@prisma/adapter-pg` for PostgreSQL to establish database connections.

faq.question: What replaced Prisma middleware and metrics?
faq.answer: The `$use()` middleware is replaced by Client Extensions, and the preview metrics feature was removed. The skill documents the replacements.

faq.question: Will this skill change my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides ordered guidance and code examples. You or the assistant apply the changes to your project.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
